samples.summary: Test named "keeps refusing a viewer PushPull write after a permitted attach" never performs an attach
samples.evidence: The test builds a fresh controller and issues a single `decide({ method: 'PushPull', verb: 'rw' })`. No `AttachDocument` call is made, and `decide()` is stateless (no session/attach state exists), so the "after a permitted attach" sequencing the name and the comment above it advertise is not exercised at all. What remains is an exact duplicate of the write half of the pre-existing 'lets a share viewer read but not write' test (lines 175-193, only the doc key differs). It therefore adds no coverage over the new READ_GATED_METHODS branch while reading, in the suite output, as if it pinned that the read-gate on attach does not leak into subsequent writes.

samples.summary: No running test verifies the empirical premise of READ_GATED_METHODS (that a real Yorkie sends AttachDocument with rw) or that a viewer link actually attaches end-to-end under enforcement
samples.evidence: The controller doc comment (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:89-92) and design doc cite `test/revision-history.e2e-spec.ts` as where attach's unconditional `rw` was 'recorded against a real Yorkie server', but that spec explicitly *omits* AttachDocument from the registered webhook method set (line 371: 'Deliberately omits `AttachDocument` from the registered set') so the attach path is never gated there. Now that the code read-gates attach, the e2e could register AttachDocument and prove a viewer attach succeeds against a real server; it does not. The only coverage is the unit test at spec line 215, which feeds a hand-written body with verb 'rw' — it pins the branch but not the premise, so if Yorkie's actual verb or method name differs (or the method is registered and something else denies), the viewer-link break this gate exists to prevent would still ship undetected.

samples.summary: New `sideTokenInjector` (no cross-side fallback, warn-and-return-undefined) has no test
samples.evidence: The delta's stated security goal is that the source secret is never used for the target and vice versa, and that a missing env var yields an anonymous (undefined) injector with a warning. No test asserts any of this: backend jest is `testRegex: ".*\\.spec\\.ts$"` (packages/backend/package.json:115) and there is no spec anywhere under packages/backend/scripts (glob of packages/backend/scripts/** returns only the three migration/copy scripts plus build artifacts). A regression that reintroduced a fallback to `process.env.JWT_SECRET` — which `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` in src/yorkie/yorkie-service-token.ts:75-87 still does by default and remains one import away — would be caught by nothing.

mergedFrom.summary: No test joins the new service-token signer to the verifier that must accept it

finding.summary: No test that `verifyYorkieToken` accepts the new `yorkie-service` token, and nothing exercises mint→verify end to end
finding.evidence: `AuthService.verifyYorkieToken` gained a third accepted `typ` (auth.service.ts:99-105), and the whole feature depends on a token minted by `signYorkieServiceToken` (yorkie-service-token.ts:38, signed with the caller-supplied `JWT_SECRET`) verifying through `AuthService` (which uses `accessSecret` = `JWT_SECRET`). The `Yorkie tokens` describe block in auth.service.spec.ts (lines 59-105) round-trips only `issueYorkieUserToken` and `issueYorkieShareToken`; I found no case constructing a service token. The controller spec cannot cover it — `makeController` stubs `verifyYorkieToken` wholesale (yorkie-auth.controller.spec.ts:22-29) and simply returns `{typ:'yorkie-service'}`. yorkie.service.spec.ts:186-190 verifies the minted token with a bare `new JwtService().verify(...)`, not through `AuthService`, so the two halves are never proved to agree. If they diverge (secret source, `typ` constant, claim shape) every server-side attach 401s on any deployment with the webhook registered — v1 content endpoints, `DocumentCopyService`, template publish/seed — and the suite stays green.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing test exists in the exact file cited. packages/backend/src/auth/auth.service.spec.ts:94-105 ("accepts a service token minted by signYorkieServiceToken") mints a token with the real signYorkieServiceToken('access-secret','10m') — imported at lines 6-9 from ../yorkie/yorkie-service-token — and verifies it through a real AuthService (makeService(), lines 64-67, configured with JWT_SECRET: 'access-secret', the same secret verifyYorkieToken reads as accessSecret), asserting typ: 'yorkie-service' and the absence of sub/shareToken. That is precisely the mint→verify end-to-end join the finding says nothing performs. Three further cases cover the same seam: :109-115 verifies the token produced by the real yorkieServiceTokenInjector (the function YorkieService passes to the yorkie.Client, yorkie.service.ts:7 / yorkie-service-token.ts:54-62); :120-127 rejects a service token signed with a foreign secret; :129-136 rejects an expired one. Nothing is mocked here — a divergence in typ constant, secret source, or claim shape between yorkie-service-token.ts:38-46 and auth.service.ts:99-105 would make these tests throw and fail. The reviewer's line range (59-105) for the describe block is stale; the block runs to line 159 in the working tree.
